w: Raised between 1508 and 1526 on a steep bluff above the Vistula in Janowiec, 14.5 km south of Pulawy, this Renaissance castle now stands in ruin, its walls still tracing the hillside site chosen for its command of the river below. A short hop across the water from Kazimierz Dolny.
s: Renaissance ruin on a Vistula bluff
_facts: Sits on a steep hillside above the Vistula in Janowiec
Located 14.5 km south of Pulawy, Lublin Voivodeship

w: Romanesque ruins dating from the 13th and 14th centuries crown the hill above Kazimierz Dolny, predating the Renaissance granaries and townhouses that later made the little Vistula town famous. Little remains but broken walls - enough to trace the outline of a castle nearly 700 years old.
_facts: Romanesque castle ruins from the 13th-14th centuries
Located in Kazimierz Dolny, Lublin Voivodeship

w: Established in 1979, this landscape park spreads across 136.70 square kilometres of ravine country in Pulawy County, folded around Kazimierz Dolny. Two separate nature reserves sit inside its boundary - the protected, wooded backdrop to the little riverside town below.
s: 136 sq km of protected ravine country
_facts: Located in Pulawy County, Gmina Kazimierz Dolny
